title: Megabits, Megabytes and Speed
objective: After this level you can work out a real download time from an advertised internet speed, and spot claims that mix up bits and bytes.
summary: Speeds are sold in megabits per second, files in megabytes. Divide by 8: a 100 Mbps line moves at most 12.5 MB a second, and typical speeds are lower.

cards.headline: Your plan says 100. Your download says 12.5. Nobody is lying.
cards.body: A 100 Mbps plan, a download bar showing about 12.5 MB a second. It looks like a rip-off. It's really a capital letter. Level 2's bits and bytes are hiding in the units.

cards.headline: Little b, big B
cards.body: Internet speeds are sold in megabits per second, written Mbps with a small b. File sizes are counted in megabytes, MB, with a capital B. And a byte, as Level 2 showed, is 8 bits. So one megabyte per second equals 8 megabits per second. To turn a speed into file terms, divide it by 8. The ad isn't wrong. It just counts in smaller pieces.

mascot.line: People mix these up all the time. Small b is bits, big B is bytes, and it takes 8 bits to make a byte.

cards.fact: A 100 Mbps line moves at most about 12.5 megabytes a second.
cards.context: So a 1 GB file, about 1,000 MB, needs at least 80 seconds, and a 100 MB game at least 8. The recipe works for any plan: divide the speed by 8, then divide the file size by the answer. Notice the words 'at most' and 'at least'. This is the best case.

cards.headline: Up to, and typical
cards.body: The number in the ad is a ceiling. Since April 2024, large US internet providers have had to show a broadband label listing typical download and upload speeds at peak hours, right beside the headline speed. So your worked-out download time is the fastest it could go. Redo the sum with the typical speed and you'll know what to expect on a busy evening, when everyone else is streaming too.

cards.headline: Speeds: decoded
learned: Speeds are in megabits (b); files are in megabytes (B)
Divide Mbps by 8 to get megabytes per second
100 Mbps is at most 12.5 MB a second
Typical speeds are lower than the advertised maximum

questions.prompt: Internet plans are sold in Mbps. What does the small b in Mbps stand for?

options.label: Bytes
options.rationale: Bytes get a capital B, as in MB.

options.label: Bandwidth
options.rationale: The b is the unit, bits.

options.label: Billions
options.rationale: Mega already means millions; b is bits.

questions.explanation: Mbps is megabits per second: a small b for bits, while a capital B means bytes.

questions.prompt: An ad says its 200 Mbps plan downloads a 100 MB game in half a second. At best, how long would it really take?

options.label: About 2 seconds
options.rationale: That divides the speed by 4, not 8.

questions.explanation: 200 Mbps divided by 8 is 25 MB a second, so 100 MB takes at least 4 seconds.

questions.prompt: Why must a speed in megabits be divided by 8 before you compare it with a file in megabytes?

options.label: Each byte is made of 8 bits, as Level 2 showed
Networks lose seven eighths of all data
options.rationale: Nothing is lost; the units differ.

options.label: A file shrinks by 8 when it downloads
options.rationale: The file stays the same size.

options.label: Internet providers round their numbers up by 8
options.rationale: The label is honest; it counts bits.

questions.explanation: A byte is 8 bits, so 8 megabits per second is one megabyte per second.
